checked_ok.claim: Android 8+ replaced the global 'Allow unknown sources' setting with the per-app 'Install unknown apps' permission, so the user grants it to the browser once.

Play Protect shows 'Play Protect hasn't seen this app before... send some info about the app to Google for scanning before you install' for unknown sideloaded APKs (page updated 2026-08-18). Hard blocks only hit SMS, notification-listener and accessibility permissions, which this app does not request.
armeabi-v7a is still supported: the React Native 0.86-stable template keeps reactNativeArchitectures=armeabi-v7a,arm64-v8a,x86,x86_64. The RN 0.84 and 0.86 release notes announce no ABI drop.
Building for two ABIs and shrinking needs no new tool: expo-build-properties has buildArchs (default is all 4 ABIs), enableMinifyInReleaseBuilds (R8) and enableShrinkResourcesInReleaseBuilds.
GitHub Releases has no bandwidth limit: 'There is no limit on the total size of a release, nor bandwidth usage'. Each file must be under 2 GiB.

Enforcement started 30 Sep 2026 and only covers participating stores in Brazil, Indonesia, Singapore and Thailand. Sideloaded installs are not checked yet (FAQ updated 2026-09-30; Android Authority correction dated 2026-10-01).
Verification expands globally to all apps on certified devices in 2027. No per-country date has been published, Turkey included.

The advanced flow is: developer mode, an anti-coaching check, a restart, then a one-time one-day (24 h) wait and biometric confirmation. After that the user can allow unverified installs for 7 days or indefinitely.
A Full Distribution account costs USD 25 ('The $25 fee for the Full Distribution account in the ADC').
For individuals, full verification needs a government photo ID plus proof of address, and an email and phone checked by OTP.
Registering a package means giving the package name and the SHA-256 certificate fingerprint, then proving ownership with an APK signed with the key.
The Limited Distribution account is free, needs no ID and is limited to 20 devices.
eas credentials can download the EAS-held Android keystore to credentials.json ('Download credentials from EAS to credentials.json').
Losing the app signing key means no more updates: 'you will not be able to release new versions of your app to users as updates to the original app'.

Still current: personal accounts created after 13 Nov 2023 must run a closed test with at least 12 testers opted in for 14 consecutive days, then apply for production access. Review usually takes 7 days or less.
An app on Play may not update itself outside Play's update mechanism. JavaScript running in an interpreter is exempt, so expo-updates OTA is allowed.
Obtainium is active: v1.6.17 was published 2026-09-13 (GPL-3.0).
GitHub's unauthenticated REST limit is still 'The primary rate limit for unauthenticated requests is 60 requests per hour', counted per IP.
Expo SDK 57 supports Android 7+ and iOS 16.4+, with compileSdk/targetSdk 36 and React Native 0.86.
StatCounter, Turkey, Sept 2026: Android versions below 7 add up to 1.82% (6.0 1.49, 5.1 0.17, 5.0 0.07, 4.4 0.07, 4.1 0.02), so about 98% run 7+.
StatCounter, Turkey, Sept 2026: iOS versions below 16.4 add up to about 2.3% (15.8 is 1.48 of that), plus 0.08% Other, so about 97.6% run 16.4+.
The EAS Free plan gives '15 Android and 15 iOS builds' per month on a 'Low-priority queue', with a 45-minute timeout and 1 concurrent build.
No Mac is needed for iPhone builds: 'iOS builds run on macOS runners hosted in Expo's macOS cloud'.
The Apple Developer Program is '99 USD per membership year'. The price is shown in local currency at enrollment.

findings.plan_quote: Android'de Google Play kapalı test kanalı da eklensin mi? Önerim: evet; GitHub APK yedek yol olarak kalır.
findings.finding: The plan treats Play as optional, and line 36 names only the GitHub APK. But device verification (line 78) relies on Play Integrity. Play Integrity's default quota is 10,000 requests per day per Cloud project. A higher quota and the optional verdict labels need the Cloud project linked in Play Console, and the higher quota also needs the app to be available on Google Play. Off-Play copies also cannot get PLAY_RECOGNIZED, so the 'app not modified' check in line 78 needs Play. At the plan's 50,000 students (about 38,500 on Android at the plan's 77%), a term-start registration wave goes past 10,000 a day, which caps a GitHub-only path. Using closed testing as the permanent channel also means tester lists (up to 200 lists of 2,000 users, or Google Groups) and a per-user opt-in. Production needs neither.

evidence.quote: Your app or SDK has a default daily limit of 10,000 total requests, tied to the associated Cloud Project Number.
To be eligible for a quota increase, your app must be available on Google Play in addition to any other distribution channels.
Projects that are enabled in the Google Cloud Console but not linked in the Play Console or Play SDK Console are not eligible for additional configuration options or quota increases.
PLAY_RECOGNIZED: The app and certificate match the versions distributed by Google Play.
You can create up to 200 lists, and each list can contain up to 2,000 users

findings.recommendation_tr: Google Play'i öneri olarak değil, Android'in ana yolu olarak koyarım. Play Console'da uygulamayı açar, Play Integrity'nin bulut projesini oraya bağlarım. Hesabın zorunlu 12 kişilik, 14 günlük kapalı testinden sonra uygulamayı mağazada normal yayına alırım; öğrenciler için test listesi tutmam. GitHub'daki APK, Google servisleri olmayan telefonlar için yedek kalır. Sebep: Play'de olmayan uygulamada Play Integrity günde 10.000 istekle sınırlı ve bu sınır artırılamıyor, dönem başı kaydına yetmez. Özet satırını da şöyle yazarım: 'Android için Google Play, Google servisi olmayan telefonlar için GitHub'daki APK.'

findings.plan_quote: Google Play de kullanılırsa aynı anahtar oraya yüklenir.
findings.finding: The intent is right, but the order matters. Play now enrolls every new app in hybrid signing with a key Google generates. You can switch to your own key only before the first release in open testing or production. Android's docs say that to use one key across stores you must give your own key at Play App Signing setup. If the default is left in place, Play installs and GitHub installs have different signatures and cannot update each other (the signing key never changes for an app). Switching channel then needs an uninstall. In this plan that counts as a device change (line 84) and loses unsent records (line 235). A separate upload key is only advised ('consider'). The same key already signs the GitHub APKs on EAS, so a second key would add work without protecting anything.

evidence.quote: Your app will be automatically enrolled in quantum-ready, hybrid signing with Google-generated keys.
Advanced developers who want to manage their own key can change this default before there is a release rolled out in open testing track or production track.

Important: If you want to use the same signing key across multiple stores, make sure to provide your own signing key when you configure Play App Signing, instead of having Google generate one for you.
As part of Android's secure update model, the signing key never changes during the lifetime of your app.

findings.recommendation_tr: Play'de uygulamayı açtığım anda, ilk test sürümünü yüklemeden önce, imza ayarından EAS'taki anahtarı 'kendi anahtarımı yükle' seçeneğiyle yüklerim. Bunu yapmazsam Google kendi anahtarını üretir; o zaman Play ve GitHub sürümleri birbirinin üstüne kurulmaz ve kanal değiştiren öğrenci için bu cihaz değişimi olur. Aynı anahtarı Play'e yükleme anahtarı olarak da kullanırım: tek anahtar, tek yedek. Play hesabına bir şey olursa GitHub yolu aynı anahtarla sürer.

findings.plan_quote: Bu yüzden tam doğrulama yaparım (kimlik ve 25 USD): paket adı ve imza anahtarının parmak izi Google'a kaydedilir.
findings.finding: With Play added (line 857), Google tells developers who distribute both on and off Play to do verification in their existing Play Console account. No separate Android Developer Console account is needed. With Play App Signing the package is registered automatically. That skips the ADC proof step, where you build and upload an extra APK carrying the registration snippet. The cost is the same one-time USD 25 Play fee. Line 859 therefore names the wrong account.

evidence.quote: Use your existing Play Console account, where there will be new functionality to register your apps outside of Google Play and keys.
If you use Play App Signing, we have the necessary information to securely identify your ownership. Your eligible apps will be part of the automatic registration process.
For existing package names, you must sign an APK with your private key and upload it. The Android Developer Console provides a snippet to add to the APK's asset folder for this challenge.
There is a US$25 one-time registration fee

findings.recommendation_tr: Google tarafında tek hesap açarım: Play Console (bir kerelik 25 USD, kimlik doğrulamalı). Geliştirici doğrulaması da bu hesaptan yapılır. Play App Signing'e kendi anahtarımı yüklediğim için paket ve anahtar kendiliğinden kaydolur; GitHub'daki APK da aynı anahtarla kapsanır. Ayrı Android Developer Console hesabı açmam. Açık noktalardaki ücret satırını şöyle yazarım: 'Apple geliştirici hesabı (yılda 99 USD) ve Google Play Console (bir kerelik 25 USD, geliştirici doğrulaması dahil).'

findings.plan_quote: GitHub APK yedek yol olarak kalır; Play sürümünde kendi kendini güncelleme olmaz.
findings.finding: The sentence implies the GitHub build updates itself, and line 510 sends an APK hash for that purpose. An in-app APK installer needs REQUEST_INSTALL_PACKAGES plus the user granting 'install unknown apps' to our app. Play forbids self-updating, and self-update is not among the permitted uses of that permission. So the plan would need two build flavors. If the update screen just opens a link (the Play page, or GitHub's permanent latest-download link), one binary serves both channels. The permission, the download and hash code and the second flavor all go away. Android already rejects an update signed with a different key, so the hash adds little.

evidence.quote: An app distributed via Google Play may not modify, replace, or update itself using any method other than Google Play's update mechanism.
Permitted uses include: Web browsing or search; OR Communication services that support attachments; OR File sharing, transfer or management; OR Enterprise device management
To link directly to a download of your latest release asset that was manually uploaded, the suffix is /releases/latest/download/asset-name.zip

findings.recommendation_tr: Uygulama hiçbir sürümde kendi APK'sını indirip kurmaz. Güncelleme ekranı Play sayfasını açar; Google servisi olmayan telefonda GitHub'daki sabit 'son sürümü indir' bağlantısını tarayıcıda açar. Böylece Play ve GitHub için tek derleme kullanılır. Ek kurulum izni, ikinci derleme türü ve sürüm kontrolündeki APK özet değeri gerekmez.

findings.plan_quote: Uygulamaları GitHub'dan kurup güncelleyen Obtainium'a pasif destek: sabit dosya adları ve "Obtainium'a ekle" bağlantısı. Ana yol yapılmaz.
findings.finding: Obtainium is active (v1.6.17, 13 Sep 2026), but it repeats the app's own version check (line 510). Its GitHub source calls api.github.com, with the token field optional. Without a token, GitHub allows 60 requests per hour per IP, so checks from shared campus addresses will fail. The 'Add to Obtainium' link is one more thing to maintain for little gain. Fixed file names are still worth keeping because they make a permanent latest-download link possible.

evidence.quote: '${await getAPIHost(additionalSettings)}/repos${standardUrl.substring('https://${hosts[0]}'.length)}'
The primary rate limit for unauthenticated requests is 60 requests per hour.

findings.recommendation_tr: Obtainium maddesini plandan çıkarırım. APK dosya adı sabit kalır; afişte ve güncelleme ekranında GitHub'ın 'releases/latest/download/<ad>.apk' kalıcı bağlantısını kullanırım. İsteyen öğrenci Obtainium'a GitHub adresini kendisi ekleyebilir; bunun için ayrıca bir şey yapmam.

findings.plan_quote: Android imza anahtarı, güncelleme imza anahtarı ve Apple sertifikaları çevrimdışı yedeklenir.
findings.finding: Of the three, only the Android app signing key cannot be replaced, and the update signing key is costly to replace. An Apple distribution certificate can be revoked and created again (EAS does this), and Apple says apps already on the App Store are not affected. Offline copies of Apple certificates are more secrets to guard with no recovery value.

evidence.quote: If your Apple Developer Program membership is valid, your existing apps on the App Store won't be affected.

findings.recommendation_tr: Çevrimdışı yedek yalnız Android imza anahtarı ve güncelleme imza anahtarı içindir. Apple sertifikası kaybolursa EAS ile yenisi üretilir; mağazadaki uygulama etkilenmez.

findings.plan_quote: Ücretsiz planda ayda 15 Android ve 15 iPhone derlemesi var, sıra önceliği düşük.
findings.finding: The quota and queue priority are correct today. What is missing is where development builds happen. Every EAS cloud build counts toward the quota. Android development builds can run on the developer's own machine (npx expo run:android). iOS has no Mac, so every iOS development build goes through EAS, and the plan's own native module (line 686) means repeated iOS builds out of 15 a month in a low-priority queue. eas build --local works only on macOS and Linux; Windows and WSL are not supported. If iOS runs out, the paid fallback is the Starter plan.

evidence.quote: 15 Android and 15 iOS builds
$19/month plus additional usage cost
macOS and Linux are supported.
compiles native code, installs the app, starts Metro

findings.recommendation_tr: Android geliştirme derlemelerini bilgisayarımda yaparım (npx expo run:android). EAS'ın ücretsiz kotası yayın derlemelerine ve Mac olmadığı için iPhone derlemelerine kalır. Yerel modül geliştirirken iPhone'un ayda 15 derlemesi yetmezse o ay Starter plana (ayda 19 USD) geçerim.

findings.plan_quote: GitHub Releases sayfasından APK indirilir ve kurulur
findings.finding: Only people with read access to a repository can see its releases. If the source repository stays private, students cannot download the APK. Bandwidth is not an issue, since GitHub sets no limit on it.

evidence.quote: Anyone with read access to a repository can view and compare releases
There is no limit on the total size of a release, nor bandwidth usage.

findings.recommendation_tr: APK herkese açık bir depodan dağıtılır. Kaynak kod gizli kalacaksa yalnız sürüm dosyaları için ayrı, herkese açık bir depo açarım.

findings.plan_quote: Kapalı test kanalı da eklenirse bilinmeyen kaynak izni ve tarama uyarısı olmaz, güncellemeler kendiliğinden gelir.
findings.finding: Play brings a recurring rule the plan does not state: every app update on Play must target an Android API level within one year of the latest major Android release (API 36 now). Expo SDK 57 targets API 36, so today is fine. With Play, though, upgrading the Expo SDK becomes a yearly obligation rather than the free choice line 526 describes.

evidence.quote: Apps must target an Android API level within one year of the latest major Android version release.
Must target Android 16 (API level 36) or higher

findings.recommendation_tr: Play kullanınca her güncelleme Google'ın hedef Android sürümü şartını sağlamalı. Bu yüzden Expo SDK'yı yılda en az bir kez yükseltirim; şu an SDK 57 bu şartı karşılıyor.

compactness_notes: Accepting F1 to F6 cuts parts on net. Removed: the in-app APK installer with REQUEST_INSTALL_PACKAGES, the APK hash in the version check and the second build flavor (F4); the Obtainium link (F5); a separate Android Developer Console account and the extra proof APK build (F3); a separate upload key (F2); offline copies of Apple certificates (F6). Added: only a Play Console app with a linked Cloud project, which the plan already recommends in line 857. No new library or tool. Keep the plan's single APK with two ABIs (arm64-v8a, armeabi-v7a) and R8 plus resource shrinking through existing expo-build-properties flags. Per-ABI APKs would make students pick the right file, and Play already splits per device from the AAB. Everything in lines 479, 516 and 522 checked out as correct and current; the findings are about the distribution path, the signing order and removable extras, not wrong facts.
open_questions: Does an app that is only in a Play closed testing track count as 'available on Google Play' for a Play Integrity quota increase? The docs do not say, so normal production release is the safe reading.
Will the source repository be public? If not, GitHub Releases cannot serve the APK to students without a separate public releases repository.

Cross-slice (device verification, line 78): copies installed outside Play cannot get PLAY_RECOGNIZED, and the plan already checks Android key attestation, which reports the package name and signing-certificate digest. Is Play Integrity needed for GitHub-installed phones at all, or only for Play installs? Dropping it for the fallback path would remove that path's quota exposure.
Does a GitHub-installed copy signed with the same key and version as the Play release get PLAY_RECOGNIZED? Not documented; worth one test once the app is on Play.
